```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
library(DT)
library(dplyr)
```

This page provides an overview of the VISTA Oncology Data Lake's evolution across multiple releases, showcasing the progressive expansion and maturation of our comprehensive cancer research platform. The data lake has grown substantially from February 2025 through August 2026, with significant increases in patient coverage, data source integration, and analytical capabilities, including the addition of whole slide imaging, detailed genomic variant data, external death records, and Neural Frame event data.

## Release Overview

The VISTA Oncology Data Lake represents a multi-institutional effort to create a comprehensive, longitudinal cancer research resource. Through systematic data releases from February 2025 through August 2026, the platform has grown from approximately 200,000 to over 220,000 patients, progressively integrating clinical OMOP data, NeuralFrame registry records, medical imaging, and molecular testing from Philips ISPM. This evolution includes specialized datasets such as the HIPPO benchmark corpus and CAP pathology forms, alongside the development of disease-specific sub-cohorts for focused research applications. The November 2025 release introduced a major OMOP 5.4 upgrade with modernized vocabularies and enhanced ETL pipelines. The February 2026 release added whole slide imaging (WSI) and a custom variant occurrence table for granular genomic data. The May 2026 release expanded WSI coverage, introduced the OMOP episode table for treatment plan analysis, and added Heme-STAMP variants to the variant occurrence table. The August 2026 release introduces several new sources including external death records, Neural Frame event data, and an expanded set of genetic variant tests (Heme-STAMP NGS/MRD, POLE, Guardant360, and the Stanford Pharmacogenomics Panel) while continuing to refresh existing sources, marking continued advancements in multi-modal data integration and research capabilities.

### Data Source Timeline

The following chart shows when each major data source became available in the data lake. Hover over any bar for details.

```{r timeline_plot, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(plotly)
library(dplyr)

timeline <- tribble(
  ~Source,                            ~Category,      ~Start,         ~End,           ~Status,
  # OMOP CDM and custom OMOP extensions
  "OMOP CDM 5.3.1",                   "OMOP",         "2025-02-01",   "2025-11-01",   "Superseded",
  "OMOP CDM 5.4.2",                   "OMOP",         "2025-11-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "OMOP Image Occurrence",            "OMOP",         "2025-02-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "Episode Table",                    "OMOP",         "2026-05-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "External Death Records",           "OMOP",         "2026-08-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "Whole Slide Imaging (WSI)",        "OMOP",         "2026-02-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "Variant Occurrence (STAMP)",       "OMOP",         "2026-02-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "Variant Occurrence (Heme-STAMP)",  "OMOP",         "2026-05-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "Variant Occurrence (Expanded Panels)", "OMOP",      "2026-08-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  # NeuralFrame Registry
  "NeuralFrame Registry",             "NeuralFrame",  "2025-02-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  "NeuralFrame Event Data",           "NeuralFrame",  "2026-08-01",   "2026-08-31",   "Active",
  # Molecular (external sources)
  "Philips ISPM",                     "Molecular",    "2025-05-01",   "2026-02-01",   "Discontinued",
  "STAMP Add-On Metadata",            "Molecular",    "2025-08-01",   "2025-10-31",   "Active",
  # Specialized Datasets
  "HIPPO Benchmark",                  "Specialized",  "2025-08-01",   "2025-10-31",   "Active",
  "CAP Forms",                        "Specialized",  "2025-08-01",   "2025-10-31",   "Active",
  "Epic Media Server PDFs",           "Specialized",  "2025-08-01",   "2025-10-31",   "Active"
) %>%
  mutate(
    Start = as.Date(Start),
    End   = as.Date(End),
    # keep tribble order top-to-bottom (reverse for plotly's bottom-up y-axis)
    Source = factor(Source, levels = rev(unique(Source))),
    Category = factor(Category, levels = c("OMOP", "NeuralFrame", "Molecular", "Specialized"))
  )

# One row per release window; sources are split into per-release blocks
release_periods <- data.frame(
  Release = c("Feb 2025", "May 2025", "Aug 2025", "Nov 2025", "Feb 2026", "May 2026", "Aug 2026"),
  RStart  = as.Date(c("2025-02-01", "2025-05-01", "2025-08-01",
                       "2025-11-01", "2026-02-01", "2026-05-01", "2026-08-01")),
  REnd    = as.Date(c("2025-05-01", "2025-08-01", "2025-11-01",
                       "2026-02-01", "2026-05-01", "2026-08-01", "2026-08-31")),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

gap_days <- 4  # inset from each release boundary to create visible gaps between blocks

segments <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(timeline)), function(i) {
  row <- timeline[i, ]
  overlaps <- release_periods[
    release_periods$REnd > row$Start & release_periods$RStart < row$End, ]
  if (nrow(overlaps) == 0) return(NULL)
  data.frame(
    Source   = as.character(row$Source),
    Category = as.character(row$Category),
    Status   = as.character(row$Status),
    Release  = overlaps$Release,
    SegStart = pmax(overlaps$RStart, row$Start) + gap_days,
    SegEnd   = pmin(overlaps$REnd,   row$End)   - gap_days,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}))

# Pastel Set3-inspired palette
category_colors <- c(
  "OMOP"        = "#80b1d3",  # sky blue
  "NeuralFrame" = "#fdb462",  # warm orange
  "Molecular"   = "#bc80bd",  # mauve
  "Specialized" = "#8dd3c7"   # mint
)

# Subtle background bands per category to visually group related rows
n <- nrow(timeline)
band_shapes <- lapply(levels(timeline$Category), function(cat) {
  rows <- which(timeline$Category == cat)
  if (!length(rows)) return(NULL)
  # y-axis is reversed, so compute row positions from the end
  y_top    <- n - min(rows) + 1 + 0.5
  y_bottom <- n - max(rows) + 1 - 0.5
  list(
    type = "rect", xref = "paper", yref = "y",
    x0 = 0, x1 = 1, y0 = y_bottom, y1 = y_top,
    fillcolor = category_colors[cat], opacity = 0.08,
    line = list(width = 0), layer = "below"
  )
})
band_shapes <- Filter(Negate(is.null), band_shapes)

fig <- plot_ly()

shown_categories <- character(0)

for (i in seq_len(nrow(segments))) {
  seg   <- segments[i, ]
  color <- category_colors[seg$Category]
  is_active   <- seg$Status == "Active"
  show_legend <- !(seg$Category %in% shown_categories)
  if (show_legend) shown_categories <- c(shown_categories, seg$Category)

  fig <- fig %>% add_trace(
    type   = "scatter",
    mode   = "lines",
    x      = c(seg$SegStart, seg$SegEnd),
    y      = c(seg$Source, seg$Source),
    line   = list(
      color = color,
      width = 22,
      dash  = "solid"
    ),
    opacity = if (is_active) 1 else 0.4,
    name        = seg$Category,
    legendgroup = seg$Category,
    showlegend  = show_legend,
    hoverlabel = list(
      bgcolor     = color,
      bordercolor = "white",
      font = list(color = "white", size = 13, family = "Arial")
    ),
    hovertemplate = paste0(
      "<b>", seg$Source, "</b><br>",
      "Category: ", seg$Category, "<br>",
      "Release: <b>", seg$Release, "</b><br>",
      "Status: <b>", seg$Status, "</b><br>",
      "<extra></extra>"
    )
  )
}

fig %>% layout(
  title = list(
    text = "<b>VISTA Oncology Data Lake \u2014 Data Source Timeline</b>",
    x = 0.02, xanchor = "left",
    font = list(size = 15)
  ),
  xaxis = list(
    title = "",
    type  = "date",
    tickmode = "array",
    tickvals = c("2025-02-01", "2025-05-01", "2025-08-01",
                 "2025-11-01", "2026-02-01", "2026-05-01", "2026-08-01"),
    ticktext = c("<b>Feb 2025</b>", "<b>May 2025</b>", "<b>Aug 2025</b>",
                 "<b>Nov 2025</b>", "<b>Feb 2026</b>", "<b>May 2026</b>", "<b>Aug 2026</b>"),
    tickangle  = -45,
    tickfont = list(size = 11, color = "#333333"),
    range = list("2025-01-01", "2026-11-01"),
    showgrid = TRUE,
    gridcolor = "#e2e2e2",
    gridwidth = 1,
    ticks = "outside",
    ticklen = 6,
    tickcolor = "#888888"
  ),
  yaxis = list(
    title = "",
    tickfont = list(size = 11, color = "#333333"),
    automargin = TRUE,
    categoryorder = "array",
    categoryarray = levels(timeline$Source)
  ),
  shapes = band_shapes,
  legend = list(
    title = list(text = "<b>Category</b>"),
    orientation = "h",
    x = 0, y = -0.18,
    bgcolor = "rgba(255,255,255,0)"
  ),
  hoverlabel = list(
    bgcolor     = "white",
    bordercolor = "#333333",
    font = list(color = "#111111", size = 13, family = "Arial")
  ),
  hovermode  = "closest",
  plot_bgcolor  = "white",
  paper_bgcolor = "white",
  margin     = list(l = 210, r = 30, t = 60, b = 90),
  height     = 560
)
```

^[**Expanded Panels** (Aug 2026): Heme-STAMP NGS/MRD, POLE, Guardant360, and the Stanford Pharmacogenomics Panel.]

### February 2025 - Foundation Release

The inaugural February 2025 release established the core OMOP 5.3.1 CDM foundation of our data lake, providing:

- **Core OMOP Dataset**: Comprehensive patient demographics, encounters, diagnoses, and procedures following OMOP CDM 5.3.1 standards
- **Clinical Infrastructure**: Essential clinical data including medications (RxNorm), laboratory results (LOINC), and procedure codes (CPT)
- **NeuralFrame Diagnoses**: Initial integration of Stanford Cancer Registry diagnosis data
- **Quality Framework**: Initial data validation and PHI scrubbing processes to ensure research readiness
- **Patient Base**: Approximately 200,000+ oncology patients forming the foundational cohort

This release prioritized data quality and standardization, establishing the structural foundation for subsequent data integration efforts.

### May 2025 - Integration Expansion

The May 2025 release marked a significant evolution with the integration of multiple specialized data sources:

- **NeuralFrame Integration**: Addition of Stanford Cancer Registry data, providing comprehensive cancer case information including diagnoses, treatments, outcomes, and miscellaneous case attributes
- **Imaging Data**: Integration of OMOP image occurrence data, linking patients to their diagnostic imaging studies
- **Philips ISPM**: Introduction of molecular testing data including STAMP, Heme-STAMP, and FoundationOne results
- **Enhanced Coverage**: Substantial increase in patient coverage across multiple data domains

This release transformed the data lake from a primarily clinical dataset to a multi-modal research platform supporting translational cancer research.

### August 2025 - Depth and Specialization

The August 2025 release focused on increasing data depth and developing specialized research capabilities:

- **STAMP Add-On Dataset**: Integrated detailed genomic testing metadata including assay types (STAMP, Heme-STAMP), pipeline versions, and test identifiers for comprehensive molecular profiling analysis
- **HIPPO Benchmark**: Added 1,394 expert-annotated clinical notes corpus for PHI identification and de-identification methodology validation
- **Lung Resection CAP Forms**: Introduced fully identified structured pathology reports combining standardized College of American Pathologists (CAP) templates with unstructured clinical information
- **Epic Media Server Documents**: Integrated all PDF documents from third-party providers accessible via EPIC Media/Lab tabs and Mulesoft API
- **Enhanced Metadata**: Expanded technical documentation including DICOM dictionary, STAMP gene panels, and genomic BED files

This release established the data lake as a comprehensive resource for both population-level and detailed clinical research, while adding critical benchmarking datasets for data quality and PHI scrubbing validation.

### November 2025 - Advanced Analytics 

The November 2025 release represents a major technical advancement with comprehensive OMOP upgrade and enhanced data capabilities:

- **OMOP 5.3 to 5.4 Upgrade**: Migrated to OMOP CDM version 5.4.2 with new tables, enhanced field linking capabilities, and updated naming conventions for improved data interoperability. This includes the addition of several new tables (not yet populated) as well as additional fields for linking between tables, along with several other minor name changes. A full description of the CDM changes can be found [here](https://ohdsi.github.io/CommonDataModel/cdm54Changes.html). 
  - **Vocabulary Modernization**: Updated from January 2023 to August 2025 OHDSI vocabulary, incorporating 2.5 years of concept mappings, domain changes, and standardization improvements
  - **Pipeline Redesign**: Overhauled ETL processes with standardized filtering (events from 2000+, flexible visit requirements) and enhanced JSON-formatted source value fields for improved data traceability
- **Genomic Tests Expansion**: Expanded Stanford test types coverage including comprehensive FoundationOne molecular profiling results
- **Agentic Tide Integration**: Advanced analytics capabilities for automated data processing and analysis

This release modernizes the technical infrastructure while maintaining backward compatibility, positioning the data lake for next-generation research applications and enhanced analytical capabilities.

### February 2026 - WSI and Genomic Expansion

The February 2026 release expands the data lake with whole slide imaging and detailed genomic variant data:

- **Whole Slide Imaging (WSI)**: Integration of manually scanned, deidentified histopathology slides stored as TIFF image files with corresponding JSON metadata. Dataset includes only slides with order_proc_ids that can be linked to Epic Clarity to ensure appropriate patient cohort inclusion and data quality
- **Variant Occurrence Table**: Custom STARR-OMOP table containing detailed genetic variant information from genomic testing. At initial release, this table included variants from STAMP (Stanford Actionable Mutation Panel for Solid Tumors) tests processed through Epic Genomics Suite starting August 2025. Coverage was later expanded in the May 2026 and August 2026 releases — see those sections for the current scope.

This release significantly expands pathology imaging capabilities and provides granular genomic variant data for translational research applications.

### May 2026 - WSI, Episode Table, and Heme-STAMP Variants

The May 2026 release further expands the data lake with additional whole slide imaging data, the introduction of an episode table, and expanded genomic variant coverage:

- **Whole Slide Imaging Expansion**: Continued integration of manually scanned, deidentified histopathology slides with expanded coverage and enriched metadata including new fields from Clarity (`specimen_received_date`, `spec_task_list` array with stainer information) and from WSI metadata (`brand`, `scanner`, `microns_per_pixel`)
- **Episode Table Introduction**: Addition of a custom STARR-OMOP episode table capturing clinical episodes representing treatment plans for patients in the oncology cohort, enabling analysis of care trajectories and treatment patterns
- **Heme-STAMP Variants**: Expanded the variant occurrence table to include Heme-STAMP test results alongside existing STAMP variants

### August 2026 - External Death Records, Neural Frame Event Data, and Expanded Genetic Variants

The August 2026 release introduces several new data sources and expands existing ones:

- **External Death Records**: Integration of `_external_death_records` table capturing deaths reported outside the EHR.
- **Neural Frame Event Data**: Addition of treatment and follow-up events from the Neural Frame cancer registry system.
- **Expanded Genetic Variants**: Broadened coverage beyond Solid tumor STAMP, including Heme-STAMP NGS/MRD, POLE, Guardant360, and the Stanford Pharmacogenomics Panel.

**Key Identifier Notes:**

- **person_id**: OMOP standard identifier used across clinical tables for patient linkage
- **person_source_value**: Source system identifier in OMOP tables that joins with stanford_patient_uid for cross-dataset linkage
- **stanford_patient_uid**: Stanford-specific unique patient identifier used in NeuralFrame and Philips ISPM datasets which is concatenation of MRN and DOB
- **MRN, DOB**: Medical Record Number and Date of Birth combination (used in February 2025 before standardization)
The transition from MRN/DOB combinations to standardized identifiers (person_id, stanford_patient_uid) in May 2025 significantly improved cross-dataset linkage capabilities and simplified cohort construction workflows.

**Additional Linkage Fields:**

- Image Occurrence table also includes **note_id**, **visit_occurrence_id**, and **accession_number** for linking to clinical notes, visits, and imaging studies

- Philips ISPM includes **accession_number** for linking genomic test results to specific clinical specimens and visits

- Whole Slide Imaging includes **accession_number** and **note_id** for linking histopathology slides to clinical notes and specimens

- Variant Occurrence includes **accession_number** for linking genomic variants to specific clinical specimens and visits, **visit_occurrence_id** for linking to clinical visits, and **procedure_occurrence_id** for linking to specific procedures associated with genomic testing

- Episode includes **person_id** for linking clinical episodes to patients in the oncology cohort

- Neural Frame Event Data uses **stanford_patient_uid** for patient linkage, along with **nfpatientsetid** (case-level identifier) and **nfpatienteventid** (event-level identifier) for linking events to specific cases

- External Death Records uses **person_id** for patient linkage, with a `death_date` field for temporal analysis of deaths reported outside the EHR

**<sup>†</sup>November 2025 OMOP 5.4 Update:** In the November 2025 release, `person_source_value` is JSON-formatted. To join with `stanford_patient_uid`, extract the field using: `JSON_VALUE(person_source_value, '$.stanford_patient_uid')`


## Multi-Release Statistical Overview

For detailed statistical analysis and interactive visualizations of data coverage trends across all releases, see the [Data Coverage Trends](may_2026/data_coverage_trends.qmd) page.
For PHI Scrubbed data coverage trends, see the [PHI Scrubbed Data Coverage Trends](deid_may_2026/deid_data_coverage_trends.qmd) page.

For each data release (February 2025 to August 2026), we examine:

- Demographic characteristics (cohort size, age distribution, gender, race)
- Data source coverage across integrated systems (NeuralFrame, Philips ISPM, Imaging, Tumor Board)
- OMOP clinical data availability (diagnoses, procedures, medications, lab results, clinical notes)
- Tumor board and thoracic sub-cohort populations with multi-modal data integration
- Imaging modality coverage and metadata diversity
- Molecular testing patterns and genomic profiling distributions
